lede: A wet Sunday in Singapore as China's vice-premier arrives for this year's top-level bilateral council, two tankers are struck in the Strait of Hormuz, and UN talks on killer robots end with countries agreeing only to keep talking.
stocks_note: Latest completed closes: New York, Friday 20 November (AAPL, GOOGL) and SGX, Friday 20 November (DBS), via Yahoo Finance. Markets reopen Monday. No earnings dates turned up in today's sources.

sections.title: Apple
sections.subtitle: Official news in brief, then 9to5Mac and MacRumors

official.label: From Apple
official.summary: Apple's last newsroom post, on 19 November, says F1 Academy, the all-female racing series run by Formula 1, will stream on Apple TV in the US from 2027, with every qualifying session and race included. It extends Apple's five-year US broadcast deal for Formula 1, which began this season. Apple's sports chief Jim DeLorenzo called the drivers the future of motorsport.

items.headline: GM brings Apple Wallet car keys to Chevrolet and GMC models in December
items.summary: General Motors is widening digital car key support in Apple Wallet. A small rollout to select Cadillacs began in late September, and many more Cadillac, Chevrolet and GMC vehicles join in December. Owners will be told in their car's app when support arrives, and GM says more models will follow over time.

items.headline: Presumed Innocent returns in February with a new story and cast
items.summary: Apple TV has renewed its 2024 legal thriller, first planned as a limited series, for a second season without Jake Gyllenhaal. Rachel Brosnahan and Matthew Rhys play a defence lawyer and her prosecutor husband on opposite sides of a murder case. It premieres on 19 February with two episodes, then runs weekly until 2 April.

items.headline: Siri AI settlement looks set to pay at least US$61 per iPhone
items.summary: Lawyers in the US class action over Apple's delayed personal Siri features told the court that claimants will probably get at least US$61 for each eligible iPhone, and up to US$95, depending on how many claims come in. Apple agreed to pay US$250 million in May without admitting wrongdoing. Claims close in about a month.

items.headline: Apple closes its Basingstoke store after more than 15 years
items.summary: Apple Festival Place in Basingstoke, England, shut for good on Saturday. Apple says every employee there can move to Apple The Oracle in nearby Reading or to another UK store. The Reading location is due to reopen as an upgraded, modernised store in December, which explains the consolidation.

items.headline: China's Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang visits for the annual bilateral council
items.summary: Ding is in Singapore on 22 and 23 November to co-chair the 22nd Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation with DPM Gan Kim Yong. PM Wong, speaking in Beijing, said the two sides expect to sign more than 20 deliverables, from trade digitalisation and financial links to healthcare and education research.

items.headline: TOUCH Preschools fires teacher after video of rough handling of a K2 pupil
items.summary: Footage sent to Stomp appears to show a teacher at HATCH by TOUCH Preschools in Hougang jerking a girl's chin several times during dance practice on 12 November. The operator says it learned of it on 16 November, suspended the three-year staff member and dismissed her the next day, and reported the case to ECDA.

items.headline: Flu jab uptake among seniors has more than doubled in five years
items.summary: Data from the Communicable Diseases Agency shows that 49.5 per cent of residents aged 65 and over had a flu vaccine in 2025, up from 20.4 per cent in 2021. Pneumococcal coverage rose from 31.6 to 67.8 per cent, and more than 199,000 shingles doses have been given since subsidies began last September.

items.headline: Cold Storage pulls a batch of NZ apple juice over a mould toxin
items.summary: After Hong Kong found patulin at 79 micrograms per kilogram in Homegrown 100% Pure NZ Apple Juice, well above the 50-microgram limit, the Singapore Food Agency had importer Cold Storage remove the one-litre bottles marked best before 11 February 2027. Anyone who has them is advised not to drink the juice.

items.headline: Khoo Teck Puat Hospital denies lapse after daughter questions father's death
items.summary: A woman wrote on Facebook that her 52-year-old father, admitted in September with eight days of high fever, was refused antibiotics and later found unresponsive before dying after a cardiac arrest. In a statement on 20 November, the hospital said there had been no lapse in his care and that staff did their best.

items.headline: US panel says China backed Pakistan in Operation Sindoor to curb India's rise
items.summary: A US congressional advisory report says Chinese military support for Pakistan during the May 2025 conflict shaped Indian planning and sharpened its security dilemma. It describes India as one of the few powers outside US alliances with the scale to compete with China, and says Beijing is working to contain it.

items.headline: India and China hold a second round of corps commander talks on Arunachal
items.summary: The Indian Express reports that Lt Gen Girish Kalia of the Army's III Corps met Chinese counterparts for close to ten days after Diwali, with a foreign ministry official present. The cordial talks aimed to set rules of engagement and lower tensions before winter, as both sides keep large troop numbers in the area.

items.headline: Amit Shah calls the Siang dam a national project and offers talks
items.summary: In his first remarks since last month's violent protests, the home minister said the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project is vital for Arunachal's development, India's energy security and strategic interests. He promised constructive discussions, a full rehabilitation package and protection of local heritage and beliefs.

items.headline: Modi and Nepal's new prime minister to launch an Ayodhya-Janakpur train
items.summary: Nepal PM Balendra Shah arrives in Delhi on his first bilateral trip abroad. On 23 November he and Narendra Modi will flag off a 604 km cross-border express linking two Ramayana pilgrimage towns, with ten stops across Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, which the railways ministry hopes will lift tourism and trade.

items.headline: India passes one crore HPV vaccinations in nine months
items.summary: The national campaign launched on 28 February to protect 14-year-old girls against cervical cancer has reached 87 per cent of those eligible. Six states, including Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, report full coverage, while Kerala and Tamil Nadu are in the mid-seventies. Uttar Pradesh alone has vaccinated more than 29 lakh girls.

items.headline: Mexico captures cartel boss 'Chapo Isidro' in a deadly raid
items.summary: Special forces, acting on US intelligence, arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, who was on the FBI's ten most wanted list, in Guasave, Sinaloa. Seven suspects and four soldiers sent as reinforcements were killed. The US accuses him of trafficking fentanyl and cocaine for decades and wants him extradited.

items.headline: Two tankers struck near Oman as Iran tightens its hold on Hormuz
items.summary: Britain's maritime monitoring agency reported tankers hit by unidentified projectiles north and east of Khasab on Saturday, with no casualties. Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted zone. The strait carried almost a fifth of world crude before the war began in February.

items.headline: Drone attack sets Russian military cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland
items.summary: The sanctioned Sparta II, heading to Kaliningrad, caught fire after two drones hit it on Saturday morning and drifted into Finnish waters. Finland's military said Ukraine was probably responsible, though Kyiv has not commented. Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said the war was spilling into Finland's neighbourhood.

items.headline: FBI investigates an apparent breach of its national crime database
items.summary: US media report that the National Crime Information Center, used by police across the country for warrants and background checks, may have been hacked. President Trump said he had just heard about it and did not like it. It follows a September breach claim by ShinyHunters and last week's string of outages.

items.headline: Bolsonaro in intensive care with a bowel obstruction
items.summary: Brazil's former president, 71 and serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup, was admitted to a Brasilia hospital on Friday with abdominal pain. Doctors say he is stable and conscious, with a stomach tube and nutritional support, but there is no discharge date. His son hinted that a tenth operation may be needed.

brief.summary: Josephine Teo told GovTech's Digital Services Awards that the public service began a systematic push six months ago to use AI for better services and more meaningful work, as residents still rate government digital services as good as private ones. Separately, Straits Interactive will bring FaceyBot, a lifelike Chinese-made robot face, to train eldercare and service staff from early 2027.

sections.title: AI startups in Singapore and Southeast Asia
sections.subtitle: Up to three stories from the past week

items.headline: Singapore's DayOne reportedly pauses its US$5 billion US listing
items.summary: The data centre operator, whose biggest customer is ByteDance, has put its planned US IPO on hold as investors question valuations for AI infrastructure, Bloomberg's sources say. DayOne filed in October with Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan among its banks, and may revisit a listing in 2027 if markets settle.

sections.title: AI worldwide
sections.subtitle: Models and products, money, policy and chips

items.headline: METR updates its widely shared chart of how long AI can work alone
items.summary: The evaluation group's revised time-horizon plot adds longer and more open-ended tasks. It finds frontier models are still improving on an exponential curve, with task length doubling roughly every four months on coding-style work, but they lag on tasks that need judgment and cannot be checked automatically.

items.headline: Hong Kong's Minds by Animoca pilots AI agents that pay on Visa
items.summary: Animoca Brands' agent platform is testing live purchases on Visa's network, letting software browse, compare and pay on a user's behalf. The pilot comes as Hong Kong regulators put agentic commerce on the policy agenda and the city pushes to make shopping agents an everyday tool.

items.headline: Actor licenses his face to a microdrama studio for a fully AI series
items.summary: Israeli actor Aki Avni let the year-old startup Shortical build a digital avatar of him for Inevitable, an AI-made microdrama that premiered in Los Angeles. AI content costs far less to produce than live action, and the practice is already common in China, though experts worry about where it leads for Hollywood.

items.headline: Nvidia reports soaring revenue while pressure grows to bring back Huang
items.summary: The chipmaker posted strong results and said former CEO Jensen Huang will not return, even as Elon Musk and others circulate a petition for him. Interim CEO Colette Kress also said Nvidia will stop selling H200 chips in China. The falling share price suggests investors are not reassured.

items.headline: Daniel Ek backs a UK fusion startup founded by an AI researcher
items.summary: Europa Fusion, set up in February by Nantas Nardelli, who worked at Google DeepMind and led machine learning at Pacific Fusion, will pursue pulsed-power fusion. It plans to lean on simulation and data rather than costly hardware. Fusion is pitched as one answer to AI's growing appetite for electricity.

items.headline: US House committee reveals licences for 880,000 AI chips sold to China
items.summary: Lawmakers published confidential records showing Washington approved nearly 880,000 advanced Nvidia and AMD chips for Chinese firms earlier this year. Analysts say the backlash could push Chinese buyers from Nvidia to AMD in the short run and speed their move to home-grown chips over time.

items.headline: UN talks in Geneva fail to agree rules on killer robots
items.summary: After a week of largely fruitless negotiations, countries agreed only to start discussing options for autonomous weapons, giving themselves two years to propose rules. The Red Cross, backed by the UN secretary-general and Pope Leo, had urged legally binding rules within a year.

items.headline: India's chief justice says banning AI in law schools is neither practical nor wise
items.summary: Speaking at a legal education conference in Hyderabad, Chief Justice Surya Kant called for a balanced approach to AI, stressing independent reasoning and academic integrity, and said no student should be found guilty on a machine's word alone. He also proposed compulsory legal aid work for law students.
